name: ghc_campaign_local_session
status: compiled and round-trip decompiled with GSC Tool 1.6.2.364; source and bytecode hashes pinned by CI; not injected or runtime-tested
behavior: Reuses only engine-created native split-screen players; validates the exact live primary/secondary pair against the current player entity array before session reuse and Campaign actions; centralized invalidation sets status 8, releases active drill/event locks, rebuilds the original level.playerpiggyback array from live player entities, preserves the previous primary when still present (otherwise the first live player), and clears stale secondary aliases; the Clockwork drill ownership helper allows one global active owner at a time and requires Stage 1 completion before Stage 2; owner may change between stages; exposes Player 2 loadout helper; never spawns or clones a player. Adds a single guarded lifecycle watcher after a successful bind; it revalidates the exact native pair and Campaign aliases every 250 ms, tolerates seven consecutive transient failures, and invalidates/releases drill ownership on the eighth failure (2 seconds). The same guarded monitor remains alive after status 8 and retries binding from a fresh engine player array every 250 ms; it never creates or clones a player. A separate stop flag permits clean monitor shutdown. Initializes the reusable 16-ID shared mission event lock after native-pair validation and aborts active event locks on rebind or stale-session invalidation while preserving completed mission events. Adds a reusable 16-ID mission event lock: one active event per local player, one owner per shared event ID, owner-only release, optional shared completion, and abort on player/session invalidation without marking completion. Different event IDs may be owned concurrently by different players; completed events persist across session rebind. Startup/rebind no longer clears level.playerpiggyback before polling; the final fallback bind requires a freshly returned live player array and reports status 2 when the fresh query is missing, preserving the previous original Campaign array without binding against stale entities. The event-lock release API also rejects an undefined or non-boolean completion flag; only exact numeric 0 or 1 is accepted, matching the host-side C contract model. The startup entrypoint also starts the guarded recovery monitor after an initial bind failure or missing player array, so a native local pair that appears later can be bound without a second manual main() call. main() now returns immediately while the recovery watcher is already active, preventing a second bounded rebind loop from racing the monitor or clearing its live aliases.
